correctness.rationale: Every private-clique vertex is simplicial and cannot lie internally on an induced path. The zero/one/two-core classification is exhaustive; nonadjacent occupied private modules forbid any core, and a two-core set with a private module requires the two neighboring core vertices of that module. These disjoint cases yield the all-set polynomial. The separate extension test classifies facets and proves their polynomial and cardinality-independent total. All seven direct induced-path brute-force instances agreed, totaling 78,848 subsets, including nonuniform modules. Boundary n=4 is excluded because antipodal core vertices have two common neighbors; finite tests supplement, not replace, the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The 2024 primary general-position-polynomial article explicitly identifies counting monophonic-position sets as a research direction. On a natural cycle-corona operation with arbitrary positive clique sizes, the theorem gives two full and self-contained polynomial enumerators, not just a scalar optimum. In particular the number of inclusion-maximal sets is independent of all module sizes while five distinct facet sizes (for uniform modules of size at least two) and an arbitrarily unbounded facet-size gap expose nonpurity. These structural facts have mathematical motivation beyond calculation or a routine single example.
